morphology.look_here_first: Confirm the perennial dioecious habit and the combination of small reniform/suborbiculate leaves with deeply crenate margins plus unisexual spikes; on pistillate material, inspect the crowded, broad, deeply lobed bracts and multifid styles.
diagnostic_traits: perennial herb or subshrub, prostrate to ascending
reniform to suborbiculate leaves with rounded/cordate bases and deeply crenate margins
unisexual inflorescences; staminate terminal, pistillate terminal and/or axillary
pistillate bracts crowded so the axis is not visible between them, with about 8–10(–13) spatulate lobes

look_alikes: Acalypha phleoides — monoecious perennial with terminal bisexual spikes; pistillate flowers below and staminate portion above on the same spike.
Acalypha persimilis / historical A. ostryifolia concept — annual, monoecious plant with different reproductive architecture and less diagnostic rounded/deeply crenate foliage.
Acalypha monostachya — local copperleaf confuser; distinguish by leaf and pistillate-bract architecture, not red coloration alone.
